# PIR-2026-001: Rack A07 lost both power feeds during planned maintenance

**Status:** Approved; action items in progress · **Blameless review:** findings describe systems and procedures, not individuals. Interactive version: [Post-Incident Review page](https://jasonmossotti.github.io/dco-vendor-scorecard/pir/).

| Incident date | Ticket | Work order | MOP | Unit | Uptime severity (OSR) | Internal severity | Priority | Incident Commander | Review meeting |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2026-09-15 | INC3900001 | WO-41023 | MOP-310 | Rack A07 | 2 Minimal | S1 (critical work without an approved MOP, finding L-004) | P1 (Landlord and IT Partner) | Customer Site Lead | 2026-09-18 |

*OSR 2 (Minimal): Some IT services disrupted or degraded, with minimal effect on users, customers, or reputation. One of 32 production racks was offline; its jobs were rescheduled onto other racks. No customer-facing service, safety, or financial loss beyond contract credits.*

## In plain language

**What happened?** During planned maintenance on one of rack A07's two power feeds, the other feed was switched off by mistake. With both feeds off, the rack lost power at 10:42 a.m. Central time. One of the 32 production racks in Hall A was offline for 4 hours 19 minutes; the rest of the site was unaffected.

**Who was affected?** The 72 GPUs in rack A07 stopped. The jobs running on them were moved to other racks by the cluster's scheduler. No other rack and no customer-facing service was affected, and nobody was hurt.

**Why did it happen?** The approved procedure covered only the feed being worked on. Nothing in it protected the second feed, whose breaker sits next to the first and looks the same, so the wrong one could be opened. When that breaker was switched back on it failed and had to be replaced, which accounts for most of the 4 hours 19 minutes.

**What are we doing about it?** The Landlord is changing its procedure so the feed that must stay on is locked and tagged before one-sided work begins, and is relabeling every breaker by rack and side. The Customer is adding an automatic alert for any rack left on one feed outside an approved window, and the handoff rule will say whether both feeds must be back before a rack is powered on. The Landlord owes contract credits for the lost power availability, and the event is under independent safety review.

## Summary (technical)

At 15:42:11Z the B-side tap-off (TO-A07-B) on BW-A-R1-PG-A2-B was opened while the A-side tap-off (TO-A07-A) was already open under MOP-310, leaving rack A07 with no input power. All 18 nodes went down within 40 seconds. The B-side tap-off unit failed on reclose and was replaced; the Landlord restored the B feed at 19:06:55Z (handoff, FA-3). The IT Partner powered on and validated the rack (rack_power_on, rack_nvlink_acceptance, nccl_allreduce_rack, all pass) and returned it to service at 20:01:36Z. The A-side tap-off stayed open until 19:22:05Z, 2 h 06 min past the MOP-310 window, so the rack was powered on (19:15:04Z) and ran on one feed until then.

- **Trigger:** Opening the B-side tap-off breaker for rack A07 while the A-side tap-off was open for planned work.
- **Detection:** Immediate: the BMS raised a P1 'Rack input power lost (both feeds)' alarm at the same second the breaker opened; the scheduler marked all 18 nodes down within 40 seconds.
- **Resolution:** B-side tap-off unit replaced and reclosed by the Landlord; rack powered on and validated by the IT Partner; A-side work completed and its tap-off closed.

## Attribution (Interface Agreement)

**Owner: Landlord** (rules FA-1, FA-3). Both of rack A07's tap-offs open from 2026-09-15T15:42:11Z to 2026-09-15T19:06:55Z (busway monitors). Under FA-3 the IT Partner's clock started at the Landlord's handoff, 19:06:55Z.

## Contract and compliance consequences

- Finding L-004 (S1): Tap-off TO-A07-B breaker opened on BW-A-R1-PG-A2-B at 2026-09-15 15:42 UTC with no approved MOP covering that asset and time.
- OT-CSL-01 Rack Power Availability measured 99.9921% against a Minimum of 99.995%: below minimum, credit $35,400.
- MOP-310 window ended 17:16:03Z; its equipment was closed at 19:22:05Z, 2 h 06 min past the approved window.

## EHS screening

- **Injuries:** 0
- **Screening:** Operating the wrong breaker on energized distribution is a hazardous-energy control concern under EHS-R2. No injury and no arc flash occurred.
- **Referral:** Referred to Customer EHS for independent investigation under the common terms; classification pending (EHS-C1 or EHS-C2).

## Contributing factors

| ID | Type | Factor |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | Procedure inadequate | MOP-310 listed only the A-side busway as an asset. It had no step to lock and tag the B-side tap-off in the closed position, and no step to verify the tap-off identity against the rack before operating. |
| F2 | Procedure not followed | The B-side tap-off was operated outside any approved MOP (finding L-004). The operation was physically possible because nothing protected the energized feed. |
| F3 | Design and identification | The A and B tap-offs for a rack sit side by side and are distinguished only by a small identifier label; there is no color or physical difference between the two sides. |
| F4 | Equipment | The B-side tap-off unit failed on reclose and had to be replaced, which turned a few-minute interruption into a 3 h 25 min outage. |
| F5 | Change control | The MOP-310 window expired at 17:16:03Z during the incident with no decision to extend or close it. The A-side tap-off stayed open until 19:22:05Z, 2 h 06 min past the window, and nothing alerted on it. |
| F6 | Procedure inadequate | HO-1 has the Customer confirm restoration from telemetry, but does not say whether one restored feed is enough. The handoff at 19:06:55Z was accepted with only the B feed closed, and the IT Partner powered the rack on at 19:15:04Z without redundancy. |

## What went well

- Detection was instant: the BMS alarm fired the same second the breaker opened.
- The Landlord acknowledged in 3 minutes and an engineer was at the equipment in 3 minutes (P1 targets: 5 and 15).
- The IT Partner acknowledged in 2 minutes and stood by for the handoff as the Interface Agreement requires (HO-1), then validated the rack in 55 minutes with every check passing first time.
- Attribution was settled from telemetry the moment the busway data was read; the Landlord's work order agreed (Landlord, FA-1), so there was no dispute.

## What went poorly

- Protection of the second feed depended on attention rather than on a lock, a tag, or a verification step.
- The MOP-310 window expired during the incident with no decision to extend it, and the rack was handed back and powered on with only one feed closed.
- The B-side operation was not reported as work outside an approved MOP; the Customer's engine found it (L-004).

## Where we got lucky

- A replacement tap-off unit was in stock (the Landlord SLA requires two per hall). Without it, restoration would have waited for a delivery.
- The error was on a single rack's tap-off. The same mistake on a busway feeder breaker would have darkened the five or six racks of a whole power group.
- The Landlord engineer was already on site for the planned work and was back in Hall A within 3 minutes.
